title: Integral representations of $f$-divergences for general von Neumann algebras
authors: Ricardo Correa da Silva, Markus B. Fröb, Gandalf Lechner, Leonardo Sangaletti
abstract: We define and analyze hockeystick divergences and $f$-divergences for normal positive functionals on general von Neumann algebras, generalizing and unifying previous work in classical probability and finite-dimensional von Neumann algebras. All the main properties of these state distinguishability measures (including in particular monotonicity, convexity, semicontinuity, bounds, state discrimination, data processing inequality) are derived from properties of the Jordan decomposition of selfadjoint normal functionals. This is done by representing the $f$-divergences as integrals over hockeystick divergences, and their significance in quantum hypothesis testing is reviewed. The $f_0$-divergence given by the information function $f_0(t) = t \ln t$ is shown to coincide with Araki's relative entropy, extending results of Frenkel to general von Neumann algebras.
summary: This paper develops a powerful generalization of classical $f$-divergences to the setting of general von Neumann algebras, using 'hockeystick divergences' as the core mathematical tool. It rigorously analyzes the properties of these quantum state distinguishability measures and aims to prove their equivalence with the relative entropy, providing deeper mathematical foundations for quantum hypothesis testing in complex physical systems.
main_problem: The paper defines and analyzes $f$-divergences and hockeystick divergences for normal positive functionals on general von Neumann algebras, aiming to generalize classical probability measures to quantum settings.
main_result: It establishes that the properties of these generalized $f$-divergences (like monotonicity and convexity) can be derived from structural properties of the underlying algebra via hockeystick divergence representations. Furthermore, it aims to prove the equivalence between this generalized $f_0$-divergence and Araki's relative entropy for general von Neumann algebras.
method: The methodology involves defining divergences using operator norms on positive functionals (hockeystick divergences) and utilizing advanced tools from functional analysis, including spectral theory, trace identities, and convergence theorems applied to unbounded operators in the context of operator algebras.
model_or_system: The mathematical framework is built upon general von Neumann algebras ($M$), which serve as a generalization of classical measure spaces. The physical states are represented by normal positive functionals ($\phi$) on $M$, relevant for quantum statistical mechanics and QFT.
key_observables: State distinguishability measures, specifically $f$-divergences and hockeystick divergences; the relative entropy ($D_{f_0}$ when $f(t)=t\ln t$).
important_parameters: The structure of the von Neumann algebra (Type I, II, or III), and limits involving regularization parameters ($\epsilon 	o 0$) used to approach infinite-dimensional structures.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of normal positive functionals on general von Neumann algebras and relies heavily on advanced theorems regarding traces and operator convergence in these non-commutative settings.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first defining hockeystick divergences as a generalization tool, then analyzing the properties of $f$-divergences derived from them. It then tackles the difficult task of proving the equivalence between these generalized divergences and established quantum information measures like relative entropy via multi-shot regularization techniques.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental mathematical tools for quantifying distinguishability between quantum states in highly general settings (infinite dimensions), which is crucial for developing rigorous theories in quantum field theory or open quantum systems where standard measure theory fails.
